en: The Apadāna of the Elder Raṁsisaññaka Hatthivagga, Number 5 I was a king named Raṁsi, a ruler of the earth. At that time, I saw the Blessed One, the Great Sage, the Teacher who had arrived at the city of Rājagaha. Having seen him, I paid homage with my head to the Buddha, the most excellent of all beings. Then, having taken up a handful of sand, I scattered it over the head of the Buddha. Because of that deed, I have been reborn here in heaven, possessing a radiance like that of the sun. By this merit, may I attain parinibbāna; may I never again be subject to birth and death. May I always be born among the gods, and from there, may I attain final liberation. Thus did the Elder Raṁsisaññaka speak of his own past deeds. The Apadāna of the Elder Raṁsisaññaka is concluded.
“Like the rising sun with its hundred rays,
like the sun with its golden beams;
like a tiger, a bull, or a noble one— ”
Well-born within the mountain range—
this is the power of the Buddha,
which shines within the mountain range.
Having gladdened my mind in Ramma,
I rejoiced in heaven for an eon;
in the remaining eons as well, I rejoiced.
A wholesome deed was performed by me;
through that clarity of mind and also through the recollection of the Buddha.
For thirty thousand aeons,
since I attained that perception then,
I have not known an unhappy rebirth.
This is the fruit of the perception of the Buddha.
In the fifty-seventh aeon,
I was once a lord of men.
Named Sujāta by name,
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
He possessed the four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā).
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Raṁsisaññaka Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Raṁsisaññaka is the fifth.
